summary.name: Orion Browser
summary.one_liner: Orion is a WebKit-based web browser from Kagi, built for speed, privacy, and compatibility with Chrome and Firefox extensions, available on macOS and iOS/iPadOS.
use_cases: browsing the web on a Mac with low resource use
private browsing without ads or tracking
using Chrome or Firefox extensions in a WebKit browser
mobile browsing on iPhone or iPad
summary.what_it_does: Orion is a web browser built on WebKit, the engine behind Safari, and is marketed for native speed and low resource use. It states compatibility with a selection of Chrome and Firefox extensions, and offers customization options and built-in Kagi services. The page describes a native macOS version and a native iOS and iPadOS version. The company says it is funded by its users rather than ads or third-party deals, and it sells access through a subscription or a one-time lifetime license under Orion Plus.
notable: Built on WebKit, the engine used by Safari, with Chrome and Firefox extension support
Funded by users with no ads or third-party deals, per the page
Available as a subscription or a one-time lifetime license via Orion Plus
caveats: Paid: offered only as a subscription or lifetime license, according to the page
Extension support is described as a curated selection, not every Chrome or Firefox extension
Listed as freeware in the awesome-mac list, which conflicts with the paid model on the page
